channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Renan Santos inicia campanha com colete à prova de balas e ataques a Lula e Flávio
item.description: Renan Santos launched his presidential campaign in São Paulo, wearing a bulletproof vest during his speech at Largo São Francisco. He attacked President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, declaring that 'enemies of the nation' will be treated as enemies and described his campaign as a 'gunpowder trail' to awaken the country.

item.title: Flavio Dino publica foto na praia e diz ser imagem de 2023
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino dismissed allegations of improper use of an official vehicle by sharing a 2023 beach photo showing him opening the door of a private car, stressing the image is old and he was not yet a minister at the time. He condemned the spread of fake news, arguing it fuels hatred and endangers public officials, and urged journalists to correct the record in the name of ethical reporting. The controversy resurfaced amid an investigation into reports by journalist Luís Pablo, who examined the use of TJ-MA official vehicles by Dino and relatives, and had his communications’ secrecy lifted by order of Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Zema abre campanha em Montes Claros e provoca Lula
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) launched his presidential campaign in Montes Claros (MG), criticizing Lula’s government and proposing 'three shocks': spending control, anti-corruption, and public security, including measures like lowering the age of criminal responsibility and building a maximum-security prison in the North. In a campaign video, he used AI and puppets to provoke Lula, depicting a paper airplane flying into Congress and landing on a Lula puppet — despite the presidential workplace being the Palácio do Planalto, not Congress.

item.title: Mário Gomes posa com Flávio Bolsonaro e pede o Exército nas ruas
item.description: Actor Mario Gomes, a federal deputy candidate, posed with Flávio Bolsonaro and advocated for military intervention in Rio de Janeiro’s streets to curb violence, referencing an armed assault on his home. He also announced an education project he intends to present to the senator, claiming Bolsonaro 'will believe in me'.

item.title: Renan Santos diz que Brasil é “nação derrotada” e promete mudança
item.description: Renan Santos, 42, businessman and co-founder of the MBL, officially launched his presidential campaign in a São Paulo rally wearing a bulletproof vest, declaring Brazil a 'defeated nation'. He promised to make Brazil one of the world's most powerful nations through a 'serious, ambitious, tough and rigid' government, emphasizing public security with war-like rhetoric and threats against criminal factions like PCC and Comando Vermelho. He stated that 'the only number that surpasses 13 is 14', seemingly referencing his electoral number or symbolically overcoming the PT (13).

item.title: Ana Estela Haddad entra na coordenação da campanha de Lula em SP
item.description: Ana Estela Haddad, Secretary of Digital Information and Health at the Ministry of Health, accepted an invitation to join the coordination of Lula's (PT) electoral campaign in São Paulo, alongside lawyer Marco Aurélio de Carvalho, founder of the Prerrogativas group. Her appointment underscores the campaign’s emphasis on digital health and information, supported by figures linked to human rights and democratic institutions.

item.title: Lula decide não ir a debate da Band e alega desigualdade de condições
item.description: President Lula's campaign announced it will not participate in the Bandeirantes TV debate scheduled for Sunday (23), citing unequal conditions to defend himself against opponents' attacks. The decision was made public on Thursday (08/16/2026) by the PT team, which argues the debate format is unfair to the incumbent candidate.

item.title: Cleitinho propõe reduzir isenções para enfrentar dívida de Minas
item.description: Cleitinho Azevedo, the Republican candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, proposed reducing tax exemptions to address the state's nearly R$200 billion debt, alongside spending cuts and fighting tax evasion. He also pledged to lower the IPVA from 4% to 3% and ease electricity and water bills, emphasizing the need to negotiate with the next Brazilian president regardless of who wins the 2026 election.

item.title: Tarcísio fala em “falsa comunicação” sobre PM perseguir Haddad
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas dismissed Fernando Haddad's claims of being pursued by military police, calling the account 'false communication' and stating that GPS data and camera footage showed no irregularities. The SSP-SP released a video showing a police vehicle passing Haddad's parked car without intervention, supporting the conclusion that no pursuit occurred.

item.title: Marçal diz que declaração de R$ 7,4 bilhões ao TSE está errada
item.description: Businessman Pablo Marçal (PRTB) claimed that his asset declaration of R$ 7.4 billion submitted to the TSE is incorrect and said he requested a correction. As of Sunday night, the 16th, he had not disclosed what the correct value should be. The statement was made in an interview with Estadão.

item.title: No dia 1 de campanha, PT faz culto à personalidade de Lula e PL projeta Flávio com antipetismo
item.description: On the first day of the 2026 election campaign, the PT held a personality cult event for Lula, emphasizing his union background and seeking to reconnect with militants through the slogan 'One like you can do more'. Meanwhile, the PL projected Senator Flávio Bolsonaro as its candidate, attempting to forge an independent identity beyond being the 'son of hope', while centering its narrative on anti-PT sentiment.

item.title: Flávio assiste à derrota do Vasco, encontra Neymar e é vaiado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL party's presidential candidate, attended Vasco's loss to Santos at São Januário stadium on Sunday, following the official launch of his campaign in Copacabana. He was accompanied by Douglas Ruas, PL's candidate for Rio de Janeiro governor, and met with Neymar before the match, during which he was booed by some fans.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vê Santos derrotar Vasco e tem camisa autografada por Neymar
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL party's presidential candidate, attended a Vasco vs Santos match in the Brazilian Championship after holding an electoral rally on Copacabana Beach. He wore a Neymar-autographed jersey and showed support for Santos during the game. The event took place following his campaign debut.

item.title: Governo Trump chama de “censura” regra eleitoral brasileira para o X
item.description: U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary for Public Diplomacy Sarah B. Rogers criticized a Brazilian electoral rule that forced X to adjust its recommendation system for the 2026 elections, calling it 'censorship imposed by Brazil'. The statement followed the platform's release of an updated algorithm to comply with local regulations.

item.title: Lula e Flávio mostram suas diferenças e duas coisas em comum no 1º dia de campanha
item.description: On the first day of the 2026 electoral campaign, Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro emphasized their differences through identity-based and legacy-driven narratives: Lula highlighted his historical ties to the working class and the PT militant base, while Flávio invoked his father Jair Bolsonaro’s legacy and the green-and-yellow symbolism seen at Copacabana. Despite the polarization, both attempted to shift toward substantive proposals for national challenges, with Lula framing his re-election bid as essential to preventing the return of Bolsonarist right-wing power, particularly citing the previous administration’s handling of the pandemic.

item.title: Eleição tem maioria de candidatos homens, brancos e empresários; veja gráficos
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian election features a majority of male candidates (65%), white candidates (48.64%), and business owners, based on TSE data updated through March 15. Women account for only 35% of candidacies, while brown and Black candidates together make up nearly 50%, despite being the majority in the electorate. The most represented age group is 45–54 years (32.52%), with candidates aged 18–24 comprising just 1.26% of total applicants.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz ter sido alvo de mais de 1,8 mil ameaças de morte
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) claims to have received over 1,800 death threats after proposing to classify PCC, CV, and militias as terrorist organizations, stating that 30 of those threats led to investigations by the Senate Police. He accuses the Lula government of inciting violence through remarks about 'traitors of the Fatherland' and says he dismissed Federal Police escort due to suspicions of PT-linked infiltrates.

item.title: Metade dos candidatos nas eleições de 2026 se declaram negros
item.description: Half of the over 20,000 candidates in the 2026 elections declared themselves as Black, totaling 49.9% when combining brown and Black declarations. White candidates accounted for 48.7%, while Indigenous and Asian candidates represented 0.9% and 0.5%, respectively. This reflects a significant increase in racial representation among Brazilian candidacies.

item.title: Vaiado em São Januário, Flávio Bolsonaro deixa estádio sem falar com a imprensa após terceiro gol do Santos no Vasco
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL's presidential candidate, was booed by Vasco fans as he left São Januário stadium after Santos scored their third goal, accompanied by Douglas Ruas and escorted by the PF. He had previously met with Neymar in the locker room and joked about the match outcome, but faced hostility despite being a Vasco supporter. Earlier, he held a campaign event in Copacabana, emphasizing change and criticizing the Lula government.

item.title: Ranking de candidatos mais ricos inclui empresário que bancou viagem de jatinho para Toffoli
item.description: Luiz Pastore (PL), candidate for first alternate on Eduardo Gomes’ Senate ticket in Tocantins, is the wealthiest candidate in the 2026 election with a declared net worth of R$ 677.74 million, according to Estadão. He owns the private jet that transported Supreme Court Minister Dias Toffoli to Peru in November 2025, shortly before Toffoli became rapporteur of the Master Case and later recused himself. Pastore, a former two-time alternate senator from Espírito Santo, switched parties and electoral domicile to run for PL in Tocantins, stating his goal is to support Brazilian entrepreneurship.

item.title: Centrão sendo Centrão: Partidos seguem estratégia ao não escolher entre Lula e Flávio
item.description: The Centrão maintains neutrality in presidential elections to prioritize winning congressional seats and become an indispensable pivot in post-election negotiations, regardless of the winner. This strategy minimizes reputational costs in polarized environments and allows local adaptation while preserving national viability.

item.title: Lula tem 58,35% contra 22,24% de Flávio no Sergipe, diz pesquisa
item.description: A poll conducted by Instituto França in Sergipe shows Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leading with 58,35% of voting intentions against 22,24% for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in a hypothetical 2026 presidential runoff. Blank and null votes totaled 11,51%, while 7,9% were undecided. The survey, carried out from August 10–12, 2026 among 2,400 voters, has a 2-point margin of error and is registered with the TSE under BR-05808/2026.

item.title: Flávio volta ao cenário da facada em Bolsonaro; Lula viaja com Alcolumbre
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula officially kicked off their 2026 electoral campaigns with events in Rio de Janeiro and São Bernardo do Campo. Flávio gathered supporters at Copacabana beach, while Lula returned to his union roots in the ABC Paulista region, where his political journey began. The campaign is now fully underway, with both candidates seeking to mobilize their electoral bases.

item.title: Tarcísio abre campanha em SP com Flávio Bolsonaro em 2º plano e foco no voto feminino
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas launched his re-election campaign with a low-profile appearance by Flávio Bolsonaro, focusing on attracting female voters. The strategy aims to balance Bolsonarist support with a more moderate and inclusive image, particularly targeting women. The article highlights Tarcísio’s effort to distance himself from explicit polarization while maintaining strategic alliances with the Bolsonaro family.

item.title: Candidato mais comum em 2026 é homem, casado e com ensino superior
item.description: The most common candidate profile in the 2026 elections is a married man with complete higher education who identifies as heterosexual. There is near parity between white and Black (black + mixed-race) candidates, and female representation reached 34.8% — the highest in historical series — though still below male candidates. For the first time, the TSE collected sexuality data: 53.1% identified as heterosexual, 2.0% as LGBTQIA+, and 44.9% preferred not to disclose.

item.title: Última delação de grande porte no STF, acordo de Mauro Cid vai completar três anos
item.description: The plea bargain of Mauro Cid, former aide-de-camp to Jair Bolsonaro, completes three years since its homologation by Minister Alexandre de Moraes at the STF, marking the last major plea deal brokered by the Federal Police at the court. Despite numerous plea proposals pending at the PGR — including those from Daniel Vorcaro (Banco Master), individuals involved in the INSS and Carbono Oculto cases — none have progressed due to investigators’ reluctance to accept grave evidence against high-ranking officials. Cid’s agreement was pivotal in the arrests of Bolsonaro, former ministers, and military commanders over their alleged role in the coup plot.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro encontra Neymar antes de jogo Vasco x Santos no Rio
item.description: PL presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro met footballer Neymar before the Vasco vs. Santos match at São Januário Stadium, following a campaign rally in Copacabana. Neymar autographed a Brazil national team jersey worn by Bolsonaro, a Vasco supporter, and also spoke with Vasco president Pedrinho. The meeting took place on the first day allowed for street campaigning, marking the start of Flávio’s official campaign agenda in Rio.

item.title: Veja as íntegras dos discursos de Lula e Flávio na abertura da campanha
item.description: The two leading candidates for President in opinion polls, Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), officially launched their electoral campaigns this Sunday in their political strongholds, marking the beginning of the 2026 election race.

item.title: Sem Kassab, Caiado começa campanha com carreata em Goiás
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, the PSD presidential candidate, launched his campaign with a motorcade in Goiás, stating his goal is to remove the PT from power and position himself as a right-wing option unaligned with Bolsonarism. He downplayed the absence of PSD president Gilberto Kassab, saying Kassab was coordinating the campaign launch in São Paulo and denied any crisis in the ticket. Caiado also reiterated he has never voted for Lula and accused the media of misinterpreting Kassab's comments about the Centrão's alleged support for Lula.

item.title: Renan Santos discursa com colete à prova de balas em ato eleitoral
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) and Amanda Vettorazzo (União Brasil-SP) spoke at an electoral event wearing bulletproof vests, criticizing Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro and stating they would direct police to 'arrest or kill' criminals. Renan said he would 'stain the ground red with the blood of these scumbags' and that the vest proves the effectiveness of their work against organized crime. Amanda declared the event marks the start of a 'spiritual and physical war' against organized crime, which will not end with an electoral victory alone.

item.title: Renan Santos ataca Lula e Flávio e promete ‘exterminar’ facções
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate for president from the Missão party, launched his campaign in São Paulo with harsh attacks on President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, vowing to 'exterminate' criminal factions through a violent confrontation strategy against organized crime.

item.title: PL foi quem mais lançou candidatos ao Congresso; PCO é o que tem mais a governador
item.description: The Liberal Party (PL) fielded the highest number of candidates for the National Congress in the 2026 elections, according to TSE data. The PCO (Workers’ Cause Party) has the most gubernatorial candidates. The official campaign began on Sunday, March 16, allowing candidates to start soliciting votes directly from voters.

item.title: Lula nunca baixou a cabeça para políticos ou banqueiros, diz Haddad
item.description: Fernando Haddad, the PT candidate for São Paulo governor, stated that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva never 'lowered his head' before politicians, bankers, or businessmen, always treating everyone equally regardless of social status. He emphasized that Lula treats workers, such as janitors, the same as billionaires, reinforcing his ties to union and popular origins. The remarks were made during Lula’s campaign launch in São Bernardo do Campo, the birthplace of the CUT and PT, as an effort to reaffirm his identity among the party’s militant base.

item.title: Novo aciona Justiça para barrar candidatura de Marçal à Presidência
item.description: Federal deputy candidate Erciley Pires Santana (New Party-GO) filed a lawsuit with the TSE to annul Pablo Marçal's (PRTB) presidential candidacy, citing missed legal deadlines, failure to submit a government plan, and challenges to the validity of Marçal's party affiliation. The action also references investigations into PRTB national president Leonardo Avalanche—Marçal's running mate—over alleged fraud and ties to the PCC. Marçal remains ineligible until 2032 due to a 2024 conviction for abuse of political and economic power, despite a provisional injunction allowing his PRTB affiliation.

item.title: Candidatos iniciam campanha presidencial em redutos eleitorais
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro launched their presidential campaigns in key electoral strongholds: Lula in São Bernardo do Campo, emphasizing his political history in the ABC region and accusing the right of responsibility for children dying without medicine and 400,000 people without vaccines; Flávio Bolsonaro began on Copacabana Beach in Rio de Janeiro. Campaign activities are permitted until October 3, one day before the first round.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro declara R$ 4,48 milhões ao TSE
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro (PL-DF), candidate for the Federal Senate, declared assets worth R$ 4.48 million to the TSE, comprising R$ 4.15 million in financial investments, R$ 300 thousand in investment funds, and a Fusca valued at R$ 30 thousand. Her candidacy was confirmed at the party convention on August 2 following reconciliation with her stepson Flávio Bolsonaro, who is running for president, after prior disputes over electoral alliances in Ceará. The registration was submitted on the final deadline of August 15, 2026, with information under the responsibility of the candidate and her party.

item.title: Assista ao discurso de Flávio Bolsonaro em ato de Copacabana
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) launched his presidential campaign at his first rally in Copacabana Beach, Rio de Janeiro, on August 16, 2026. In a 34-minute speech, he urged supporters not to give up on Brazil, criticized the current president for alleged incompetence and corruption, and praised his father, Jair Bolsonaro, as an honest and unjustly treated leader, leading the crowd in chanting 'Volta Bolsonaro' as a tribute.

item.title: Renan Santos lança candidatura à Presidência em SP: "Guerra até o fim"
item.description: Renan Santos officially launched his presidential candidacy for the Partido Missão in an event held at Largo São Francisco, in front of the USP Law School in São Paulo. In a confrontational tone, he declared he would not celebrate but demand 'more, more, more' until defeating opponents such as Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula, aiming for a runoff in the 2026 elections. He also announced Guto Schiavetto as his Senate candidate for São Paulo.

item.title: A avaliação de Tarcísio sobre a suspeita de perseguição a motorista de Haddad
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas dismissed claims that a driver for Fernando Haddad was followed by police vehicles, stating investigations indicate a 'false crime report'. He said GPS data and footage from 70 cameras showed the patrol cars followed normal routes without stopping or engaging the vehicle. The driver will be summoned to testify, as Haddad prepares to challenge Tarcísio in the 2026 election.

item.title: Foi a última vez que o Lula enganou os brasileiros, diz Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, PL presidential candidate, declared in Copacabana that it was the 'last time' Lula 'deceived the Brazilian people', calling the president a 'hope deadbeat' and unveiling his 'tesouraço' plan to cut taxes, bureaucracy, and reduce the age of criminal responsibility. He criticized Lula's economic management, citing rising living costs and high femicide rates, and labeled the PT candidacy as the 'path of darkness'.

item.title: Patrus abre campanha ao lado de Lula: "Ganhar em MG é ganhar o Brasil"
item.description: Minas Gerais gubernatorial candidate Patrus Ananias (PT) joined President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election campaign launch in São Bernardo do Campo, stating that 'winning in Minas is winning Brazil'. He emphasized the state’s strategic importance and announced that Lula will visit Belo Horizonte on Friday (21/8) to officially launch his gubernatorial campaign, alongside running mate Jarbas Soares and senatorial candidates Marília Campos and Áurea Carolina.

item.title: As eleições na cidade onde Bolsonaro venceu Lula por um voto
item.description: In Nanuque, Minas Gerais, Bolsonaro defeated Lula by just one vote in the 2022 presidential elections. Four years later, Mayor Gilson Coleta Barbosa believes the right will widen its advantage in the 2026 elections, despite the strong influence of Bolsa Família in the city. Local elections remain tightly contested but peaceful, with symbolic disputes such as who brings more cars to the caravans.

item.title: Janja canta jingle de Lula com pastor evangélico
item.description: First Lady Janja participated in a campaign event for Lula's re-election in São Bernardo do Campo, where she spoke and then invited evangelical pastor Kleber Lucas to sing the campaign jingle alongside her. The performance was accompanied by a music video, highlighting the campaign's outreach to religious and popular sectors.

item.title: José Dirceu: ‘Lula tem que fazer campanha como se estivesse perdendo’
item.description: José Dirceu, former Chief of Staff and PT candidate for federal deputy in São Paulo, argues that President Lula must campaign as if he were losing, stressing direct voter engagement in everyday spaces like family, work, and church. Despite undergoing lymphoma treatment, Dirceu remains optimistic about a fourth Lula term, citing the broad center-left coalition and internal PT unity as key advantages.

item.title: Eleições de 2026 têm apenas duas mulheres entre 13 presidenciáveis
item.description: Out of 13 presidential candidates in Brazil's 2026 elections, only two are women, accounting for 15% of the total. These female candidates are not among the frontrunners in polling, highlighting the ongoing underrepresentation of women in the race for the nation's highest office.

item.title: Se eleição fosse hoje, Tarcísio venceria no 1º turno em SP, diz Vox
item.description: A Vox Brasil poll shows Tarcísio de Freitas would win the São Paulo gubernatorial election in the first round with 53.7% of voter intentions, ahead of Fernando Haddad at 34.0%. In a potential runoff, Tarcísio leads with 54.3% against Haddad's 35.2%. Haddad leads in rejection at 46.1%, while Tarcísio's rejection stands at 22.3%.

item.title: ‘O problema do Brasil é que bandido fica solto’, critica Romeu Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential candidate for the Novo party, launched his campaign in Montes Claros with a focus on public security, stating that Brazil's problem is that 'criminals go free'. He promised to build a 'superprison' in the North for criminal faction leaders and criticized the STF, alleging that ministers grow rich while the people become poorer, citing the R$ 129 million contract of Alexandre de Moraes' wife. Zema also highlighted his Minas Gerais management as a model of prosperity without corruption and argued that Brazil is not a failed country, but a robbed one.

item.title: Um dia depois de deixar o PL para apoiar Paes, Romário já participa de carreata com o ex-prefeito
item.description: Senator Romário left the PL to support Eduardo Paes (PSD) in the Rio de Janeiro mayoral race, participating in a motorcade through the Baixada Fluminense one day after leaving the party. Although he did not post about it on social media, he appeared in a photo shared by Paes’ campaign. His move drew criticism from the PL, which threatens expulsion under a national resolution banning elected officials from supporting candidates of other parties, particularly given his past shifts in allegiance in 2022 and 2024.

item.title: Em ato, Flávio usa camiseta com a frase “O Brasil vai vencer”
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), presidential candidate, held his first campaign rally at Copacabana Beach in Rio de Janeiro, wearing a green and yellow shirt with the slogan 'Brazil will win' and a bulletproof vest. During his speech, he repeated the slogan, and his wife, Fernanda Bolsonaro, wrote it with lipstick on his back. The event included allied politicians and emphasized the symbolic messaging of the Bolsonaro campaign.

item.title: Juliano Spyer lança 'O Brasil dos Evangélicos' em São Paulo
item.description: Anthropologist and Folha de S.Paulo columnist Juliano Spyer launches his new book 'O Brasil dos Evangélicos' in São Paulo with a book signing at Livraria da Vila on Paulista Avenue at 6 p.m. on Monday, the 17th. The work examines the influence of evangelical movements in Brazilian society and politics.
